rows.speaker: قراء أهل الحجاز والمدينة والبصرة
rows.claim: The Hijazi, Medinan, and Basran readers lighten the fāʾ, making Zakariya the one who took Maryam into his care; they connect this wording with 3:44.
rows.anchor: به القارئون ذلك بتخفيف الفاء

rows.speaker: قراء الكوفيين
rows.claim: The Kufan readers read the fāʾ doubled, meaning God made Zakariya Maryam’s guardian.
rows.anchor: الكوفيين: {وكفلها زكريا} [آل عمران: 37]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the doubled fāʾ: God assigned Maryam to Zakariya by the lot and sign that made him prevail over his rivals, so his custody followed God’s judgment.
rows.anchor: مشددة الفاء بمعنى: وكفلها الله زكريا

rows.speaker: بعض أهل العلم
rows.claim: One account says Zakariya’s lot stood still while the other lots were carried by the river, indicating that he had the strongest claim to Maryam.
rows.anchor: فقال بعض أهل العلم: رتب قدح زكريا، فقام فلم يجر به الماء وجرى بقداح الآخرين الماء

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another account says Zakariya’s lot went upstream while the others flowed downstream and disappeared, marking him as the one entitled to her.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل صعد قدح زكريا في النهر، وانحدرت قداح الآخرين مع جرية الماء وذهبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whichever account of the lots is correct, al-Ṭabarī says God decreed Maryam’s custody for Zakariya over the other claimants; Zakariya took her by God’s award.
rows.anchor: وأي الأمرين كان من ذلك فلا شك أن ذلك كان قضاء من الله بها لزكريا على خصومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appeal to the light reading of 3:44 does not prove that this verse must also be light: one can say that God made Zakariya her guardian by His judgment in the lot.
rows.anchor: فحجة دالة على ضعف احتيال المحتج بها

rows.speaker: قراء المدينة
rows.claim: The general Medinan readers lengthen the name Zakariyya, while the general Kufan readers shorten it; al-Ṭabarī calls both established languages and readings with the same meaning.
rows.anchor: قرأته عامة قراء المدينة بالمد، وقرأته عامة قراء الكوفة بالقصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both long and short forms of Zakariya are sound, widespread readings and do not differ in meaning, so either is correct.
rows.anchor: وهما لغتان معروفتان وقراءتان مستفيضتان في قراءة المسلمين، وليس في القراءة بإحداهما خلاف لمعنى القراءة الأخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the lengthened form, Zakariyya is accusative without nunation as a foreign proper name; on al-Ṭabarī’s doubled-fāʾ reading, it is the direct object of the verb.
rows.anchor: اسم من أسماء العجم لا يجرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third form, Zakariy without the long vowel and silent yāʾ, is not recitable because it conflicts with the Muslim codices, though Arabic treats it like a nisba form and declines it.
rows.anchor: وفي زكريا لغة ثالثة لا تجوز القراءة بها لخلافها مصاحف المسلمين وهو زكري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rajaz line uses kāfil for one who gathers stray animals and takes them into his care; the alternate wording evokes straying or fleeing animals.
rows.anchor: يعني به: تضمها إليك وتأخذها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabic question “Why do you take every stray?” illustrates kafala as taking a stray animal in and keeping it.
rows.anchor: يقال منه للرجل: ما لك تكفل كل ضالة؟ يعني به: تضمها إليك وتأخذها

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima reports that the lots flowed with the current except Zakariya’s pen, which rose upstream, and he consequently became Maryam’s guardian.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة، في قوله: {إذ يلقون أقلامهم أيهم يكفل مريم}

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabi explains that Zakariya took Maryam in; the contestants cast staffs toward the current, and Zakariya’s staff faced it and defeated theirs.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه، عن الربيع، قوله: {وكفلها زكريا}

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi relates that Torah scribes used lots to choose who would raise a child brought to them; Zakariya, whose wife was Maryam’s aunt, won the contest and took her into his house, the sanctuary.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، قال الله عز وجل: {فتقبلها ربها بقبول حسن

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses the phrase as Zakariya taking Maryam in with him.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة: {وكفلها زكريا} [آل عمران: 37] يقول: «ضمها إليه»

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says Zakariya’s lot was determined by his own pen.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {وكفلها زكريا}

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Maryam was the daughter of their chief and prayer leader; the scholars contested custody, drew lots, and Zakariya, her sister’s husband, raised her in his home.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: " كانت مريم ابنة سيدهم وإمامهم

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima recounts that Maryam’s mother dedicated her daughter to the temple; after the leaders disputed custody and drew lots with their Torah pens, Zakariya prevailed and took her.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة، قال: " ثم خرجت بها يعني أم مريم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Zakariya placed Maryam with him in his sanctuary.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " جعلها زكريا معه في محرابه

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj explains that “kahin” in their speech means a learned person.
rows.anchor: قال حجاج: قال ابن جريج: الكاهن في كلامهم: العالم

rows.speaker: محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq’s report through Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr stresses that Maryam was orphaned after both her father and mother, then recounts her and Zakariya’s story.
rows.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، عن محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير: {وكفلها زكريا}

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says Maryam was with Zakariya, who placed her in his sanctuary.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قوله: {وكفلها زكريا}

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the people drew lots over Maryam, Zakariya won, and he became her guardian.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {فتقبلها ربها بقبول حسن وأنبتها نباتا حسنا}

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: An alternative account says Zakariya first cared for Maryam without a contest, keeping her with her aunt after her parents died; much later, hardship led others to draw lots to divide her maintenance, not from rivalry for her.
rows.anchor: غير أن القول متظاهر من أهل التأويل بالقول الأول

rows.speaker: شعيب الجبئي
rows.claim: Shuʿayb al-Jubbaʾi reports that Yahya’s mother, Maryam’s aunt, was named Ashiʿ.
rows.anchor: عن شعيب الجبئي، " أن اسم أم يحيى: أشيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the no-lot account would support the light reading if true, al-Ṭabarī prefers doubling the fāʾ because the dominant exegetical account places the lots before Zakariya’s custody and says he won over his rivals.
rows.anchor: غير أن القول متظاهر من أهل التأويل بالقول الأول أن استهام القوم فيها كان قبل كفالة زكريا إياها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains that whenever Zakariya entered the sanctuary where he had placed Maryam, he found provision from God for her nourishment; reports identify it as fruit out of season.
rows.anchor: وفاكهة الصيف في الشتاء ذكر من قال ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the provision as grapes in a basket, found outside their season.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {وجد عندها رزقا} [آل عمران: 37] قال: «وجد عندها عنبا

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the provision was grapes appearing out of season.
rows.anchor: عن عطاء، عن سعيد، في قوله:

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrahim glosses the provision as fruit appearing outside its season.
rows.anchor: عن إبراهيم، في قوله: {وجد عندها رزقا}

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says Maryam had summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer.
rows.anchor: عن الضحاك، «أنه كان يجد عندها فاكهة الصيف في الشتاء

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says Zakariya found grapes at Maryam’s place in their off-season.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: «كان يجد عندها العنب في غير حينه»

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid also describes the gift as summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {وجد عندها رزقا}

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says they used to relate that Maryam received winter fruit in summer and summer fruit in winter.
rows.anchor: قال: «كنا نحدث أنها كانت تؤتى بفاكهة الشتاء في الصيف

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Maryam was found with fruit outside its usual season.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة: {وجد عندها رزقا}

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says Zakariya placed seven doors around Maryam and found summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer when he entered.
rows.anchor: عن الربيع، قال: «جعل زكريا دونها عليها سبعة أبواب

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Zakariya kept Maryam in the sanctuary and found each season’s fruit at the opposite time of year.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، قال: «جعلها زكريا معه في بيت وهو المحراب

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says Zakariya found summer fruit in winter.
rows.anchor: سمعت الضحاك يقول في قوله: {وجد عندها رزقا}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the provision as fruits of Paradise, with summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {كلما دخل عليها زكريا المحراب وجد عندها رزقا}

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq transmits from some learned authorities that Zakariya found winter fruit in summer and summer fruit in winter.
rows.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال: ثني بعض أهل العلم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the provision came from heaven and not from people; the report reasons that if Zakariya knew its source, he would not have asked Maryam about it.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن، قال: " كان زكريا إذا دخل عليها - يعني على مريم - المحراب وجد عندها رزقا من السماء من الله، ليس من عند الناس

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another view says the provision was an excess beyond what Maryam’s appointed caretaker brought her, rather than food appearing miraculously from heaven.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل معنى ذلك أن زكريا كان إذا دخل إليها المحراب وجد عندها من الرزق

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq relates that during famine Zakariya could no longer maintain Maryam; the Israelites also struggled, so they drew lots to assign her maintenance, and the lot fell to a carpenter named Jurayj.
rows.anchor: محمد بن إسحاق، قال: " كفلها بعد هلاك أمها، فضمها إلى خالتها أم يحيى

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: In Ibn Ishaq’s account, the carpenter Jurayj brought food from his earnings, but God increased it inside the sanctuary; Maryam urged him to trust God, and Zakariya found the extra provision and asked its source.
rows.anchor: قال: فعرفت مريم في وجهه شدة مؤنة ذلك عليه، فكانت تقول له: يا جريج، أحسن بالله الظن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī defines the mihrab as the foremost and most honored place in an assembly or prayer place, including a mosque; its plural can be maḥārib as well as maḥārīb.
rows.anchor: وأما المحراب فهو مقدم كل مجلس ومصلى، وهو سيد المجالس وأشرفها وأكرمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The line by ʿAdī ibn Zayd compares ivory figures in mihrabs with bright eggs in a flowered meadow, illustrating the word’s sense of honored prayer places.
rows.anchor: كدمى العاج في المحاريب أو كال … بيض في الروض زهره مستنير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī gives both al-maḥārīb and al-maḥārib as plurals of mihrab.
rows.anchor: والمحاريب جمع محراب، وقد يجمع على محارب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariya asks Maryam where or by what means she got the provision he sees; she answers that God sent and gave it to her.
rows.anchor: يعني بذلك جل ثناؤه: قال زكريا يا مريم: أنى لك هذا؟ من أي وجه لك هذا الذي أرى عندك من الرزق

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says Zakariya shut seven doors, entered, and repeatedly found fruit out of season, prompting his astonished question to Maryam.
rows.anchor: أنه كان فيما ذكر لنا يغلق عليها سبعة أبواب، ويخرج ثم يدخل عليها، فيجد عندها فاكهة الشتاء في الصيف

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq transmits a similar account: Zakariya was amazed to find the seasons’ fruits reversed and asked Maryam where they came from.
rows.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال: ثني بعض أهل العلم، فذكر نحوه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Zakariya found fresh fruit with Maryam when no one else had any, so he asked her where it came from.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {يا مريم أنى لك هذا قالت هو من عند الله}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God provides whoever He wills without measure: giving does not diminish His store or change His dominion, and unlike a limited giver, He neither fears depletion nor lacks knowledge of what He gives.
rows.anchor: فخبر من الله أنه يسوق إلى من يشاء من خلقه رزقه بغير إحصاء ولا عدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” refers to the reports about Imran’s wife, Maryam, Zakariya, Yahya, and the events narrated from the account beginning with God’s choosing Adam and Noah.
rows.anchor: {إن الله اصطفى آدم ونوحا} [آل عمران: 33] ثم جمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means hidden reports about earlier people, unknown to Muhammad and his community and known only to a few learned people among the two scriptural communities.
rows.anchor: فقال: هذه الأنباء من أنباء الغيب: أي من أخبار الغيب، ويعني بالغيب، أنها من خفي أخبار القوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God says He revealed these hidden accounts to Muhammad as evidence of his prophethood and truthfulness, removing the excuse of People of the Book who knew how obscure the reports were.
rows.anchor: ثم أخبر تعالى ذكره نبيه محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه أوحى ذلك إليه حجة على نبوته، وتحقيقا لصدقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their obscurity supports the proof: Muhammad was unlettered, did not read books, and did not learn these accounts from companions among the People of the Book.
rows.anchor: إذ كان معلوما عندهم أن محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم أمي لا يكتب فيقرأ الكتب فيصل إلى علم ذلك من قبل الكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī derives ghayb as the verbal noun of ghāba, to be absent from or hidden from something.
rows.anchor: وأما الغيب: فمصدر من قول القائل: غاب فلان عن كذا، فهو يغيب عنه غيبا وغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here nuḥīhi means “We send it down to you.”
rows.anchor: فإن تأويله: ننزله إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basic sense of waḥy is conveying something from the one who communicates it to its recipient; this can occur through writing, gesture, indication, inspiration, or a messenger.
rows.anchor: وأصل الإيحاء: إلقاء الموحي إلى الموحى إليه، وذلك قد يكون بكتاب وإشارة وإيماء وبإلهام وبرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 16:68, God’s waḥy to the bees means that He inspired them.
rows.anchor: بمعنى: ألقى ذلك إليها فألهمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 5:111, God’s waḥy to the disciples means that He inspired or communicated the knowledge to them.
rows.anchor: بمعنى: ألقيت إليهم علم ذلك إلهاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rajaz phrase about God’s waḥy to people to praise morning and evening illustrates conveying a command, potentially by indication.
rows.anchor: بمعنى: فألقى ذلك إليهم أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 6:121, the devils’ waḥy to their allies means whispering or casting a suggestion to them.
rows.anchor: يلقون إليهم ذلك وسوسة، وقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 6:19, the Qur’an was conveyed to Muhammad by Gabriel from God.
rows.anchor: ألقي إلي بمجيء جبريل عليه السلام به إلي من عند الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun waḥy names what passes from sender to recipient; Arabs also call script and writing waḥy because the written words are fixed in what is inscribed.
rows.anchor: وأما الوحي: فهو الواقع من الموحي إلى الموحى إليه، ولذلك سمت العرب الخط والكتاب وحيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr’s line says poems remain like waḥy on hard stone, illustrating waḥy as writing fixed in its medium.
rows.anchor: أتى العجم والآفاق منه قصائد بقين بقاء الوحي في الحجر الأصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic can call a book waḥy, without the alif, when a scribe has written and embellished it; Ruʾba’s line about a finely written Gospel illustrates this usage.
rows.anchor: كأنه بعد رياح تدهمه … ومرثعنات الدجون تثمه إنجيل أحبار وحى منمنمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idh yalqūn means “when they were casting”; their aqlām were the lots or arrows used by the Israelites to decide who would care for Maryam, as explained at 3:37.
rows.anchor: وأما أقلامهم فسهامهم التي استهم بها المتسهمون من بني إسرائيل على كفالة مريم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the statement that Muhammad was not present refers to Muhammad himself.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {وما كنت لديهم}

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says Zakariya and his companions drew lots with their pens for Maryam when she was brought to them.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد: {يلقون أقلامهم} [آل عمران: 44] «زكريا وأصحابه استهموا

words: إِذْ يَلْقُونَ أَقْلَٰمَهُمْ أَيُّهُمْ يَكْفُلُ مَرْيَمَ
rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada recounts that Maryam, daughter of their leader, became the subject of a custody dispute; the Israelites drew lots, Zakariya won, and as her sister’s husband he took her in.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {وما كنت لديهم إذ يلقون أقلامهم أيهم يكفل مريم وما كنت لديهم إذ يختصمون}

words: إِذْ يَلْقُونَ أَقْلَٰمَهُمْ أَيُّهُمْ يَكْفُلُ مَرْيَمَ
rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada also summarizes the contest as drawing lots over Maryam, with Zakariya winning the right to care for her.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {يلقون أقلامهم} [آل عمران: 44] قال: «تساهموا على مريم أيهم يكفلها، فقرعهم زكريا»

words: إِذْ يَلْقُونَ أَقْلَٰمَهُمْ أَيُّهُمْ يَكْفُلُ مَرْيَمَ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says worshippers in the sanctuary, who wrote revelation, cast their pens to choose who would care for Maryam; God told Muhammad he had not witnessed their dispute.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وما كنت لديهم إذ يلقون أقلامهم أيهم يكفل مريم}

words: إِذْ يَلْقُونَ أَقْلَٰمَهُمْ أَيُّهُمْ يَكْفُلُ مَرْيَمَ
rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says they cast lots with their pens to determine who would care for Maryam, and Zakariya beat the others.
rows.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {إذ يلقون أقلامهم أيهم يكفل مريم}
